cases.description: Noise-free Gaussian (sigma 6x4, theta 0) released by stage B: alpha=4 D4 sigma matches analytic 4*sigma*0.9986568.
cases.derivation: d4 = 4*sigma*T(alpha=4) with T=0.9986568: 4*6*0.9986568=23.9678, 4*4*0.9986568=15.9785; alpha=4 vs alpha=6 delta is below the 3 percent floor so stage B is released.

cases.description: Same Gaussian rotated by theta=0.6: alpha=4 D4 sigma stays rotation-invariant.
cases.derivation: The truncation factor depends on alpha, not orientation; rotated pixel sampling is slightly noisier, hence the wider tolerance.

cases.description: The 2D Gaussian fit recovers amplitude, sigmas and center of a clean noise-free Gaussian.
cases.derivation: A noise-free Gaussian is exactly reproducible by the fitted model; LM converges to the generating parameters up to grid discretization.

cases.description: Seeded-noise Gaussian at SNR 100 (sigmaB=1, fixed literal seed) releases stage B inside the documented release band.
cases.derivation: SNR 100 sits inside the 15/15 release oracle; D4 is the alpha=4 analytic value plus a small seed-noise moment bias, pinned on the generator-identical run.

cases.description: Core plus 1 percent amplitude halo at 4x width, noise-free: alpha-consistency suppresses stage B.
cases.derivation: The single-Gauss fit absorbs the halo width and the alpha=4 vs alpha=6 delta is about 14 percent against the 3 percent noise-free floor (re-measured, gate-calibration spec).

cases.description: Two separated beams (main 200 counts sigma 6, satellite 26 counts sigma 3 at 44 px): residual gate fails first, multi-peak still counts 2.
cases.target: analyzeImage / multi-peak count and gate precedence
cases.derivation: PIN CORRECTION (first run): the 26-count satellite alone leaves uncorrelated-fit residual RMS sqrt(26^2*pi*9/9216)=1.44 counts, above the 0.005*peak=1 ceiling, so the documented precedence reports residual_high; all gates are still evaluated and the satellite (26 > 0.1*peak, 44 px > 2*(2*sigmaMajor)) pins significantPeakCount 2.

cases.description: Gaussian (sigma 8, center x=72) on a 96-wide frame: the 6-sigma check ellipse leaves the ROI and the clipping gate suppresses.
cases.derivation: Check-ellipse half-extent is 6*sigma=48; centre 72+48=120 exceeds the right ROI boundary 95, so the clipping gate suppresses before alpha and multi-peak.

cases.description: Compact Gaussian whose tails under the mask floor are exactly 0 at the ROI rim: sigmaB is exactly 0, so the alpha MC is skipped with 3 percent floors.
cases.derivation: maskBelowCounts=1 forces every rim pixel to exactly 0, so rim MAD/IQR and the dtype floor are 0 and sigmaB is exactly 0; the documented skip-MC contract gives thresholds 3, count 0, decimation 1 and EVT arm 0.

cases.description: Seeded Gaussian at sigmaB=3 on a 96x96 ROI: the multi-peak EVT arm and scanned pixel count are pinned.
cases.derivation: PIN CORRECTION (first run): evt = sigmaB_est*(sqrt(2 ln 9216)+0.5) with the rim-MAD estimate 2.9340 counts for this seeded geometry (not exactly 3), so the measured pin is 14.0035; the formula itself is exact in the estimated scale.

cases.description: Released noise-free Gaussian (sigma 6x4, theta 0.3): ellipticity is the axis ratio sigmaMinor/sigmaMajor.
cases.derivation: Analyzer ellipticity is sigmaMinor/sigmaMajor = 4/6 = 0.6667; the alpha=4 truncation cancels in the ratio.

cases.description: A wide beam whose 6-sigma release ellipse fits the frame while the 9 and 12 sigma wing probes do not: the absorbed-power detector reports the reach it actually had.
cases.derivation: The probe ellipse of alpha sigmas is used only when its bounding box lies inside the ROI. For sigma 20x12 at 0.3 rad the half-extent in x is alpha*sqrt((20*cos0.3)^2+(12*sin0.3)^2) = alpha*19.44 px, so alpha=6 needs 116.6 px of the 149.5 px available and alpha=9 needs 175.0 px and is dropped. maxAvailableProbeAlpha therefore reads 6, not the nominal 12, and the frame releases with the reduced reach stated rather than implied.

cases.description: A beam on a uniform pedestal the fit absorbs: stage A measures a ROI-sized sigma, the cross-tier check cannot run, and the result says so instead of staying silent.
cases.derivation: Stage A moments the whole ROI, so a uniform pedestal contributes its own variance W^2/12: with beam power 2*pi*1000*36 = 226195 and pedestal power 100*10000 = 1e6, the mixture variance is (226195*36 + 1e6*833.25)/1226195 = 686 px^2, sigma_A = 26.20 px and 4*sigma_A = 104.8 px, past the 100 px shorter ROI side. The fit absorbs the pedestal into its constant term, so stage B is unaffected and releases; the check that would have compared the two tiers simply has no usable tier A, which is what the block reports.

cases.description: Released noise-free Gaussian (sigma 6x4): encircled-power radii for fractions 0.5 and 0.8 of the ANISOTROPIC beam.
cases.derivation: PIN CORRECTION (first run): the circular law 1-exp(-r^2/(2*6^2)) does NOT apply to the anisotropic 6x4 beam; integrating F(r)=(1/(48*pi))*int_0^2pi (1-exp(-r^2*(9-5cos^2(phi))/288))/(2e(phi)) dphi gives F(5.8309)=0.50 (refined from the measured run) and F(9.2)=0.80.
